body.objective: Determine whether the Einstein-like metric-plus-phase sector of the complex-compensator theory closes under the first nonlinear interactions or necessarily sources additional fourth-order modes.
body.stop_condition: Import the complete action-derived complex-compensator classical BV parent and its contraction by exact hashes. Derive q2, q3 and the first required q4 identity directly from the single action, transfer them cyclically to the reduced g_hat-plus-theta model, and compute the branch-resolved tensors in exact Einstein-image, additional-Weyl, phase-clock and Maxwell coordinates. Test every mixed channel needed to decide E/theta/Maxwell closure, including resonant (+lambda,-lambda)->0 and homogeneous charge channels. Prove whether pi_X q_n(E/theta/Maxwell,...) vanishes, is exact/removable under the complete admissible cyclic L_infinity redefinition family, or gives an invariant nonzero cohomology/deformation class. Join surviving sources to the Taub moment map and bounded-resonance ledger. If the Einstein phase closes only on a constrained cone, state that cone exactly; if it fails, exhibit the first source coefficient and independent verifier.
body.current_gate: branch-resolved nonlinear closure or sourcing theorem for the compensator Einstein phase
body.forbid: no vertex copied from strict Weyl or the old Berger action; no retained representative called invariant before deformation-cohomology reduction; no vanishing selected coefficient called branch closure; no one-particle absence used to dismiss a physical interaction; no formal secular correction called stability; no anomaly, quantum, particle, scattering or unitarity promotion
activates: an interaction-level verdict for the emergent Einstein phase
body.resource_hint: COMPENSATOR NONLINEAR CONSUMER. First compute the sparse branch mixing table; only then attempt a broad transferred minimal model. An invariant source of the extra branch is as valuable as closure.
notes: The Einstein phase is a sector of a changed theory, not the strict pure-Weyl Einstein image.
Use the invariant metric and the reduced phase field after the radial quartet contraction.
Keep formal extendibility, bounded continuation and stability as separate lifecycles.
